summary: Security group rule sgr-0123456789abcdef0 on sg-0abc123def456789 allows inbound TCP/22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH management access on network interface eni-0123456789abcdef0 to the entire internet.

evidence.detail: is_egress=false, ip_protocol=tcp, from_port=22, to_port=22, peer.type=ipv4, peer.value=0.0.0.0/0

reasoning.description: Rule sgr-0123456789abcdef0 permits inbound tcp/22 from source 0.0.0.0/0 (all IPv4 addresses).
Network interface eni-0123456789abcdef0 is a member of security group sg-0abc123def456789 and has a public IP address, making it internet-reachable.
Combining steps 1-2: an arbitrary internet host can reach SSH (tcp/22) on eni-0123456789abcdef0, independent of any NACL evaluation.

assumptions: The security group is currently attached to a running, internet-facing workload rather than an unused/placeholder interface.
limitations: This finding evaluates the Security Group layer only. A Network ACL deny rule (stateless, evaluated independently -- see firewall-rule.aws-nacl-deny-inbound.json) could still block some or all of this traffic; NACL evaluation was out of scope for this rule and is not represented in this finding's verdict.
remediation: Restrict source_ranges on sgr-0123456789abcdef0 to known management CIDRs (e.g. a corporate VPN or bastion range) instead of 0.0.0.0/0, or require access via AWS Systems Manager Session Manager instead of a routable SSH port.
